main_deity: Kṛṣṇa and his two wives Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā
description_en: Rādhākṛṣṇa Mandira is located to the north of the confluence of the rivers Vāgmatī (Bagmati) and Viṣṇumatī. Nowadays, the junction of these rivers is known as Ṭeku Dobhāna, however, the old name is Cintāmaṇi Tīrtha. The temple features a unique hybrid style; its largeśikharatower is supported by the maincella,whilst its circumambulatory path has been constructed using carved timber columns and cross beams and is covered by a tile skirting roof.According to a report by the Nepal Department of Archaeology, the temple was established in 1887 CE (VS 1944) by the stepmother (kānchī āmā) of Deva Śamśera.  A document dated 1894 (VS 1951) which is preserved in the Guṭhī Saṁsthāna archives refers to this temple and itsguṭhīlands.The temple suffered severe damage during the 2015 earthquakes. The brick walls at the four corners of thecellapartly collapsed due to a combination of poor maintenance and ineffective repairs made in the past. It was discovered that the timber framework of the interior bearing structure had mostly rotted away and was not properly repaired in a restoration effort around 2007. The four timber corner posts embedded in the walls had also completely deteriorated. A detailed damage assessment carried out by national and international structural experts under the aegis of UNESCO revealed that 90 percent of the temple's timber structure was in urgent need of replacement. The complex structural build-up of timber frames integrated in the brickśikharatower would have madein siturepairs extremely difficult and rendered the building at a high risk of collape in the future. It was therefore decided that repairs should be made by dismantling the temple and rebuilding it from the ground up. The original materials were to be used whenever possible. Reconstruction works commenced in July 2019 and were completed in 2021.The sanctum houses a stone statue of Kṛṣṇa, flanked by his consorts Rukminī and Satyabhāmā. Kṛṣṇa is playing the flute and his consorts are depicted in the midst of a dance. A stone pillar stands in front of the temple with a tortoise at its bottom and a statue of a praying Garuḍa on top. According to local informants, the original Garuḍa statue was stolen and recently replaced with a smaller statue of inferior quality.According to a report by the Nepal Department of Archaeology, the temple was established in 1887 CE (VS 1944) by the stepmother (kānchī āmā) of Deva Śamśera.
description_ne: काठमाण्डौं उपत्यका भित्रका नदी दोभानहरूलाई हिन्दू–बौद्ध दुबै समुदायले तीर्थस्थल मान्दै आएका छन् । तीर्थस्थल मानी उपत्यकाका नदीहरूका संगमस्थलमा विभिन्न मन्दिरहरू निर्माण गरिएको पाइन्छ । बागमती र विष्णुमती नदीको संगमस्थललाई टेकु–दोभान भन्ने गरिएको छ । उपत्यकामा लेखिएका बौद्ध ग्रन्थहरूमा यस दोभानलाई ''चिन्तामणि तीर्थ'' पनि भनिएको पाइन्छ । यही दोभानमा यो मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । चार तहको पेटीमाथि बनेको मन्दिर पूर्वाभिमुख छ । गर्भगृहभन्दा माथिको भागमा झिंगटीको छाना बनेको छ जसलाई टुंडालहरूले थमाइएको छ । छाना माथिको संरचना शिखर शैलीमा उठाइएको छ । यसर्थ यो मन्दिरलाई मिश्रित शैलीको मान्न सकिन्छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृह भित्र बीचमा कृष्ण र उनको दायाँ–बायाँ रुक्मिणी र सत्यभामाको मूर्ति रहेको छ । मन्दिर अगाडि एक शिलास्तम्भ खडा छ जसमाथि गर्भगृहतिर फर्की नमस्करण मुद्रामा बसेका गरुडको मूर्ति रहेको छ । पुरानो गरुड चोरी भएपछि हाल राखिएको मूर्ति नयाँ हो ।वि.सं. १९५१ मा यस मन्दिरको निम्ति छुट्याइएको जाग्गाको लगत राखिएको अभिलेख गुठी संस्थानमा पाइएको छ । गत भूकम्पले निकै क्षति पुगेपछि हाल मन्दिर पुनःनिर्माणको क्रममा रहेको छ । मन्दिरमा पौड्याल थरका ब्राह्मण विहान नित्य पूजा र बेलुकी आरती दिनका लागि गुठी संस्थानबाट नियुक्त छन् । मन्दिरको वर्षवर्धन पूजा वैशाख शुक्ल दशमीका दिन हुने गरेको छ । कृष्णजन्माष्टमी (भदौ कृष्ण अष्टमी)का दिन मन्दिरमा विशेष पूजा गरी रातभर जाग्राम बसी व्रत बस्ने परम्परा चल्दै आएको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: New statues of Kṛṣṇa, Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā donated
historical_events.event_description: New statues of Kṛṣṇa, Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā were made and installed. Funds were collected from local people and the current priest's father had contributed Rs. 3,000.

The Department of Archaeology restored the temple in circa 2007. There are undated photographs documenting the restoration process in the collection of the DOA, however, no reports or other documents pertaining to the work could be found.
The statue of Rukmiṇī was stolen.
The statue of Rukmiṇī which was stolen in 2012 was replaced with a new one.
The monument was seriously damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.

Rādhākṛṣṇa Mandira was restored from ground-up between 2019-2021. The UNESCO Kathmandu Office and the Department of Archaeology managed the restoration with funding from Hainan Chang Foundation (China).
